column2: (for example, you chose an Illusion token and find the split card Illusion/Reality)
column3: Outdated: the ruling (published 2008-10-01, Shards of Alara) gives as its example an Illusion token sharing a name with the split card Illusion // Reality, from when a token whose name the effect creating it didn't specify was named after its subtypes alone. Since the Innistrad: Crimson Vow rules update (the CR effective 2021-11-19; Wizards' "Comprehensive Rules Changes" of 2021-11-10 names this very interaction), such a token is named after its subtypes plus the word "Token" (CR 111.4: "If the spell or ability doesn’t specify the name of the token, its name is the same as its subtype(s) plus the word “Token.”"), so an Illusion token is named "Illusion Token" and Clarion Ultimatum finds no Illusion // Reality for it. Only this example is outdated: the rest of the ruling (a nonpermanent card found stays in the library) is cited in tests/rulings/r_p191_resolution.rs (clarion_ultimatum_only_finds_permanent_cards). See docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md.
